sections.h2: Only 15 of 141 auctioned coal mines were producing by June 2026

chart.title: Most of the drop comes between allocation and opening permission
chart.sub: Commercial coal mines from rounds 1 to 14, by status at 30 June 2026 (number of mines).
chart.source: Ministry of Coal reply in Parliament, August 2026.

sections.means: Of the 141 mines auctioned, 109 allocated mines still lacked permission to open, so most of the gap sits before production.
sections.todo: Publish a block-by-block schedule against which the ministry's milestone deadlines can be checked.

sections.h2: Bidders offered 24.17% of coal value, six times the 4% floor

chart.title: Average bid revenue share sits far above the 4% floor
chart.sub: Share of the value of coal, %.

sections.means: Bids this far above the floor show demand for the blocks, but they say nothing about whether the mines produce coal.
sections.todo: Publish how often performance security has been appropriated for missed milestones, and how much has been collected.

sections.h2: Captive and commercial mines' output share rose from 10.9% to 20.2%

chart.title: Most of that coal comes from captive blocks, not commercial auctions
chart.sub: Share of India's coal output, captive and commercial mines combined, %.

sections.means: The combined group produced a record 210 million tonnes, while the commercial mines added only about 26 million.
sections.todo: Report commercial-only output each year beside the combined figure, so the two series are not mixed in public statements.
